rows.stem: In plants, the role of cytokinin is to/in :

options.label: A
options.text: promote cell division

options.label: B
options.text: wilting of leaves

options.label: C
options.text: promote opening of stomatal pore

options.label: D
options.text: growth of stem

rows.solution:
Cytokinins promote cell division, which is why they are present in greater concentration in areas of rapid cell division, such as fruits and seeds. Wilting of leaves is linked to abscisic acid, and growth of the stem to auxins and gibberellins.

This is option (A) promote cell division.

rows.stem: The number of chromosomes in parents and offspring of a particular species undergoing sexual reproduction remains constant due to :

options.label: A
options.text: doubling of chromosomes after zygote formation.

options.label: B
options.text: halving of chromosomes after zygote formation.

options.label: C
options.text: doubling of chromosomes before gamete formation.

options.label: D
options.text: halving of chromosomes at the time of gamete formation.

rows.solution:
In sexual reproduction two germ cells fuse to form the zygote. If each germ cell carried the full set of chromosomes, the number would double in every generation. So the germ cells are made by a special type of division that halves the number of chromosomes, and when two of them fuse, the zygote gets back the full number found in the parents.

This is option (D) halving of chromosomes at the time of gamete formation.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Ozone \((\mathrm{O_3})\) gas at higher levels of atmosphere is a product of UV radiation acting on Oxygen \((\mathrm{O_2})\).

**Reason (R) :** The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in 1980s.
rows.context: For Questions number 8 and 9, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
At the higher levels of the atmosphere, ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms, which combine with oxygen molecules to form ozone:

\(\mathrm{O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} O + O}\)

\(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\)

So the Assertion is true. The amount of ozone in the atmosphere did begin to drop sharply in the 1980s, which is linked to synthetic chemicals such as CFCs, so the Reason is true as well.

But the fall in the ozone level does not explain how ozone is formed. Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.stem:
In the following food chain, 5 J of energy is available to man. Calculate, how much energy was available at the producer level. Why ?

Plant \(\longrightarrow\) Goat \(\longrightarrow\) Man
rows.solution:
Only about 10% of the energy available at one trophic level is transferred to the next (the 10 per cent law); the rest is used up by the organisms at that level in their life processes or lost as heat.

Working back from the man:

Energy at the goat level \(= 5 \times 10 = 50\) J.

Energy at the producer (plant) level \(= 50 \times 10 = 500\) J.

So 500 J of energy was available at the producer level.

rows.stem:
A blue colour flower (BB) bearing plant is crossed with a plant with white coloured flowers (bb).

(a) State the colour of the flowers you would expect in their \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny.

(b) What must be the percentage of white flower plants in the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation, if the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated ?

(c) State the expected ratio of genotypes BB and bb in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny.
rows.solution:
(a) Blue is the dominant trait. Every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant gets B from one parent and b from the other, so all are Bb, and all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants bear blue flowers.

(b) Parents: BB \(\times\) bb. Gametes: B and b.

\(\mathrm{F_1}\): Bb (blue).

Selfing the \(\mathrm{F_1}\): Bb \(\times\) Bb. Each plant gives gametes B and b, and the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) combinations are:

| | B | b |
|---|---|---|
| **B** | BB | Bb |
| **b** | Bb | bb |

So the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has BB : Bb : bb in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1, that is 3 blue : 1 white. Only bb plants are white, so the percentage of white flower plants is \(\dfrac{1}{4} \times 100 = 25\%\).

(c) BB : bb = 1 : 1, since each appears once among the four combinations.

rows.stem: Which of the following compounds will undergo addition reaction ?

options.label: B
options.text: \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\)

options.label: C
options.text: \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\)

options.label: D
options.text: \(\mathrm{CH_4}\)

rows.solution:
An addition reaction takes place only in an unsaturated compound, one with a carbon-carbon double or triple bond. \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\) fits the general formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\) of the alkenes (butene), so it has a double bond and adds hydrogen or other reagents across it. \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\), \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\) and \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) fit \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\), the saturated alkanes, which undergo substitution, not addition.

This is option (B) \(\mathrm{C_4H_8}\).

rows.stem:
Comment on the following properties of ionic compounds and give reason in support of your answer :

(i) Physical nature

(ii) Melting and boiling points
rows.solution:
(i) Physical nature: ionic compounds are solids and are somewhat hard, because of the strong force of attraction between the positive and negative ions. They are generally brittle and break into pieces when pressure is applied.

(ii) Melting and boiling points: ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points, because a considerable amount of energy is required to break the strong inter-ionic attraction.

rows.stem:
Give reasons :

(i) Potato chips manufacturers fill the packet of chips with nitrogen gas.

(ii) Respiration is an exothermic reaction.

(iii) Silver chloride is stored in dark coloured bottles.
rows.solution:
(i) The packets are filled with nitrogen to prevent the oils and fats in the chips from being oxidised. Oxidised fats turn rancid and change the smell and taste of the chips; nitrogen is an unreactive gas, so it keeps oxygen away.

(ii) During respiration, glucose combines with oxygen in the cells of our body and energy is released:

\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6(aq) + 6O_2(aq) \rightarrow 6CO_2(aq) + 6H_2O(l) + energy}\)

A reaction in which energy is given out is exothermic.

(iii) Silver chloride decomposes into silver and chlorine in sunlight:

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

A dark coloured bottle keeps light out and so prevents this decomposition.

rows.stem: In an electric circuit carrying current \(I\), a \(2\,\Omega\) resistor is replaced by an \(8\,\Omega\) resistor without changing the connected (ideal) battery. Then :

options.label: A
options.text: current becomes \(\frac{I}{4}\) and potential difference \(\frac{V}{4}\)

options.label: B
options.text: current becomes \(\frac{I}{4}\) and potential difference remains \(V\)

options.label: C
options.text: current becomes \(4I\) and potential difference remains \(V\)

options.label: D
options.text: current becomes \(4I\) and potential difference \(\frac{V}{4}\)

rows.solution:
The stem does not define V. It is read as the potential difference across the resistor, which here is that of the ideal battery; the battery is not changed, so the potential difference stays V.

By Ohm's law, \(I = \dfrac{V}{R}\). With V fixed, the current is inversely proportional to the resistance. The resistance goes from \(2\,\Omega\) to \(8\,\Omega\), four times as much, so the new current is \(I' = \dfrac{V}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{V}{2} = \dfrac{I}{4}\).

This is option (B) current becomes \(\frac{I}{4}\) and potential difference remains \(V\).

rows.stem: Redraw the following ray diagrams in your answer book and show the path of reflected/refracted ray :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the two diagrams to redraw: (i) a concave mirror with pole P and the points F and C marked on the principal axis in front of it, and one ray travelling parallel to the principal axis towards the mirror; (ii) a concave lens with optical centre O and the points \(\mathrm{F_1}\) and \(\mathrm{2F_1}\) marked on the principal axis to its left, and one ray travelling parallel to the principal axis towards the lens from the left. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(i) Concave mirror: a ray parallel to the principal axis, after reflection, passes through the principal focus F. Redraw the mirror with C, F and the pole P on the principal axis. From the point where the incoming ray meets the mirror, draw the reflected ray back towards the object side so that it passes through F, and continue it beyond F. Mark arrows on both rays.

(ii) Concave lens: a ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction, diverges and appears to come from the principal focus \(\mathrm{F_1}\) on the same side of the lens as the incoming ray. Redraw the lens with O, \(\mathrm{F_1}\) and \(\mathrm{2F_1}\) on the principal axis. From the point where the ray meets the lens, draw the refracted ray going on to the right and bending away from the principal axis. Produce it backwards as a dotted line to meet the principal axis at \(\mathrm{F_1}\). Mark arrows on the rays.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem:
Study the given diagram and answer the questions that follow :

(a) Write the name of the eye defect shown in the diagram. Where is the image formed in this eye defect with respect to the retina of the eye ?

(b) List two causes of this eye defect.

(c) With the help of a ray diagram, show how this defect of vision is corrected.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the defect exists only in the drawing: an eye (lens and eyeball) receiving parallel rays from points marked O and O' far in front of it (O' drawn with dashed lines), the rays meeting at a point inside the eye; where that point lies relative to the retina is withheld here since it decides the defect. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
(a) The defect is myopia (near-sightedness). The parallel rays from the distant object meet inside the eyeball, so the image is formed in front of the retina instead of on it.

(b) Two causes:

1. Excessive curvature of the eye lens.

2. Elongation of the eyeball.

(c) Myopia is corrected with a concave lens of suitable power. Diagram: draw the eye and place a concave lens in front of it. Parallel rays from a distant object (O' at infinity) fall on the concave lens and diverge, so that they appear to come from the far point O of the myopic eye; produce the diverging rays backwards as dotted lines to meet at O. The eye lens then focuses these rays on the retina. Mark arrows on the rays and label the concave lens, O, O' and the retina.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
(i) Write the name and statement of the rule used to determine the direction of the :

(I) force experienced by a straight current-carrying conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field.

(II) magnetic field produced around a straight conductor carrying electric current.

(ii) Differentiate between the magnetic field due to a bar magnet and the magnetic field due to a current-carrying solenoid.
rows.solution:
(i) (I) Fleming's left-hand rule. Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force acting on the conductor (its direction of motion).

(II) The right-hand thumb rule. Imagine holding the current-carrying straight conductor in the right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.

(ii) Any one difference:

1. The strength of the magnetic field of a bar magnet is fixed, while that of a current-carrying solenoid can be changed by changing the current through it (or the number of turns).

2. The direction of the field of a bar magnet cannot be changed without turning the magnet round, while the direction of the field of a solenoid is reversed simply by reversing the direction of the current.

3. A bar magnet is a permanent magnet, while a solenoid behaves as a magnet only as long as the current flows through it.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-carrying Conductor
rows.stem:
(i) With the help of a diagram, describe an activity in brief to show that a current-carrying straight conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

(ii) Two straight current-carrying conductors (A) and (B) are shown in the figures below :

(I) Mark the direction of the magnetic fields around these current-carrying conductors (A) and (B).

(II) Compare the strengths of magnetic fields produced (1) at points P and Q and (2) at points Q and R due to these current-carrying conductors, qualitatively.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (ii) gives the two conductors only as a drawing: (A) a vertical straight wire carrying I = 1 A through the centre O of a circle, with point P on the circle 2 cm from O; (B) a vertical straight wire carrying I = 2 A through the centre O of two concentric circles, with Q on the inner circle 2 cm from O and R on the outer circle 4 cm from O. The direction of each current is given only by arrowheads and is withheld here, since it decides (ii)(I). Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
(i) Activity: take a long straight thick copper wire and connect it in series with a battery, a plug key and a rheostat. Hold a small compass close to the wire, below or beside it, with the wire lying along the needle. Close the key.

Observation: the compass needle is deflected as soon as the current flows. Reversing the direction of the current deflects the needle the other way, and switching the current off brings the needle back to its north-south position.

Conclusion: a compass needle is deflected only by a magnetic field, so the current-carrying straight conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

Diagram: draw the circuit with the battery, the key, the rheostat and the straight wire, the compass near the wire with its needle deflected, and arrows showing the direction of the current.

(ii) (I) By the right-hand thumb rule the field lines are concentric circles around each wire.

Conductor (A): the current of 1 A flows upwards, so the field lines run anticlockwise when seen from above. Mark the arrows on the circle through P in that sense.

Conductor (B): the current of 2 A flows downwards, so the field lines run clockwise when seen from above. Mark the arrows on both circles, through Q and through R, in that sense.

(II) The magnetic field of a straight conductor increases with the current and decreases as the distance from the wire increases.

(1) P and Q are both 2 cm from their wires, but the current in (B) is 2 A against 1 A in (A). So the magnetic field at Q is stronger than at P (about twice).

(2) Q and R lie around the same wire carrying 2 A, but R is 4 cm away and Q only 2 cm. So the magnetic field at Q is stronger than at R (about twice).
